messages.text: how comprehensive is the testing so we can see if everything works as expected

I am assessing the repo's current test coverage and how much confidence it actually gives. First I am locating the test suites, test commands, and any CI config so I can judge breadth, gaps, and whether everything works as expected is realistically covered.

Testing is reasonably broad at the unit and service layer, but it is not comprehensive enough to say everything works as expected across the whole product. There are about 214 test and spec files in the repo, with the API package carrying most of the coverage. PR CI does run unit tests and builds as hard gates, so this is not an untested repo. The weak point is system coverage: Playwright exists, but it is small and not always blocking. The biggest gaps are missing explicit coverage thresholds, separate DB-backed integration paths that are not part of the normal PR unit job, thin mobile coverage, and relatively light testing in shared and UI packages.
can you make a plan to expand and improve the test suite to validate teh product end to end

I am grounding this in the current test architecture and product surfaces so the plan targets real gaps rather than generic add more tests. Next I am inspecting the existing E2E specs and the main app routes and flows they cover to define what an end to end validation plan should include.

Build a unified E2E program across web, API-backed workflows, and mobile, with the explicit goal of validating real user journeys and side effects rather than page presence. Start by getting the current automated test and smoke layers reliably green, then expand from that stable baseline into deterministic seeded environments, stronger browser journeys, API workflow coverage, and a narrower first mobile E2E slice. The plan should make critical business journeys block PRs once stabilized, while broader cross-browser and device coverage runs on branch and nightly tiers.
